note: Every claim below is checked against a generated artifact by scripts/validate-claims.py, which runs as the last step of `make verify`. A claim whose check fails is a build failure, not a downgrade to 'unverified'. Claims not marked 'verified' may not appear in the README, on Devfolio, in the video, or in social copy -- the validator enforces that too.

claims.text: All 18 assertions in the unmodified upstream test suite pass against the Zig library.
claims.limitation: upstream/pdjson/tests/tests.c is compiled in place from the pinned tree and linked against zig-out/lib/libpdjson.a. No copy is made and no line is edited; scripts/verify-upstream-hashes.sh enforces byte-identity independently.

claims.text: Zero assertions in the upstream suite are skipped, adapted, or marked unsupported.
claims.limitation: The suite contains 18 assertions. Passing them is necessary, not sufficient -- which is why the differential corpus exists.

claims.text: The upstream source tree is byte-identical to commit 78fe04b across all 9 files.
claims.limitation: Verifies the committed copy against a SHA-256 manifest. scripts/fetch-upstream.sh re-clones from GitHub at the pinned commit to confirm the copy matches the real upstream.

claims.text: Across 1,926 differential comparisons on the fixed corpus, the Zig implementation and the pinned C original produce byte-identical behaviour transcripts, with 0 divergences.
claims.limitation: 214 inputs x 9 drive modes. Counts only inputs where the original has defined behaviour; the 43 cases where an ASan+UBSan build of the original reports an error are counted separately as upstream_ub (see C-06) and are not folded into this number.

claims.text: The differential comparison covers 9 drive modes including peek, skip, reset, the separator API, strict mode, and 4 deterministic allocation-failure schedules.
claims.limitation: Modes are next, nostream, peek, skip, sep, oom:0, oom:1, oom:2, oom:5. Documented in docs/transcript-schema.md.

claims.text: Differential testing found a null-pointer dereference and an out-of-bounds read in the pinned original, both at pdjson.c:912, reachable through the public API under allocation failure.
claims.command: make differential && cc -fsanitize=address,undefined -I upstream/pdjson -o /tmp/r tests/upstream-bugs/repro_oom_stack.c upstream/pdjson/pdjson.c && /tmp/r
claims.limitation: Confirmed against the pinned upstream by ASan and UBSan, with a minimal public-API reproducer in tests/upstream-bugs/repro_oom_stack.c. Analysis in docs/upstream-bug-oom-stack.md. Reported upstream; the issue URL is recorded in artifacts/upstream-issues.json.

claims.text: The memory-buffer source in the pinned original treats byte 0xFF as end-of-input on signed-char targets, disagreeing with its own FILE* source on identical input.
claims.limitation: 0xFF is never valid UTF-8, so this changes which error is reported, the byte position, and whether json_source_get() can advance -- it does not make the parser accept invalid input. Analysis in docs/upstream-bug-0xff.md.

claims.text: The Zig static library contains exactly one Zig-compiled object, exports all 22 public symbols from the pinned header, and contains no upstream parser code.
claims.limitation: Checks archive membership, absence of pdjson.c's 23 internal symbols, absence of undefined json_* imports, presence of all 22 exports, and that no Zig build input references pdjson.c.

claims.text: The Zig declarations and the pinned C header agree on every struct offset, size, alignment and enumerator, with sizeof(struct json_stream) == 272 on this target.
claims.limitation: Verified on the host target (arm64 macOS) and in CI on x86-64 Linux. Both tables are derived from the same header on each side, so the check tracks the platform's C ABI rather than hard-coding one; it attests only to targets it has been run on.

claims.text: A C program that includes the pinned public header and declares struct json_stream by value links against only the Zig archive and passes its checks.
claims.limitation: tests/original/abi_consumer.c exercises events, depth, context, raw number lexemes, number values, error text, line numbers, streaming with reset, skip, and json_isspace.

claims.text: The shipped library uses no @constCast, no inline assembly, no @setRuntimeSafety, no unreachable, and no force-unwraps; its 10 pointer casts are confined to the C allocator and char* boundaries and are individually enumerated.
claims.limitation: Zig has no 'unsafe' keyword, so the report defines the term explicitly and lists every occurrence with file and line. Scope is src/ -- the shipped library. Budgets are exact, so an increase requires editing the scanner.

claims.text: The shipped artifact is built in ReleaseSafe, so bounds checks and overflow checks are active at runtime, including in the reported benchmark figures.
claims.limitation: A bare `zig build` produces ReleaseSafe by design (DECISIONS.md D-10). ReleaseFast numbers are reported alongside, not instead.

claims.text: All 12 deliberately injected defects in the Zig implementation are detected by the fixed-corpus differential, with zero survivors.
claims.limitation: Cases where an ASan+UBSan build of the original reports an error are excluded from the comparison, because every mutant trivially differs there. Earlier runs that did not exclude them produced a false 12/12; see DECISIONS.md D-17.

claims.text: Both transcript producers are deterministic: five runs over every fixture in five modes produce byte-identical output.
claims.limitation: Transcripts deliberately exclude pointer values, heap addresses, timing, and errmsg bytes past the NUL terminator, none of which are reproducible. See docs/transcript-schema.md.

claims.text: The Zig implementation's json_get_number matches C strtod bit for bit across a 661-point exponent sweep, powers of two, digit strings up to 500 digits, 20,000 randomised decimal lexemes and 20,000 randomised hex floats.
claims.limitation: Asserted by tests/port/number_torture.zig, which fails the build on any mismatch; the artifact reference here is a proxy because Zig's test runner does not emit JSON. Two documented exceptions: nan(...) payloads that overflow 64 bits are implementation-defined per C99 7.20.1.3p4 and are not matched (D-09). The hex-float path is implemented in this project rather than delegated, because std.fmt.parseFloat truncates past 53 bits of mantissa -- found by fuzzing at ~30M cases (D-18).

claims.text: The Zig implementation is slower than the C original on 9 of the 12 benchmark workload/mode pairs measured, and faster on 3.
claims.limitation: This is an honest mixed result, not a win. Ratios are C median / Zig median on arm64 macOS, 5 repetitions, binaries interleaved within each repetition, all raw per-iteration samples in bench/results/raw.json. The one large Zig win (malformed-early) is dominated by setup rather than parsing and should not be read as throughput. Methodology and the profiling that explains the remaining gap are in bench/methodology.md.

claims.text: A published differential fuzz session found zero divergences, zero crashes and zero timeouts.
claims.limitation: Exact duration, seed, case count and rate are recorded in the session log referenced by artifacts/verification-report.json. Allocation-failure modes are excluded from the default fuzz modes because the original crashes constantly there; they are covered exhaustively by the fixed corpus and by tests/port/allocator_failure.zig instead.

claims.text: Behavioural equivalence has been demonstrated for the buffer input source; the FILE* and user-callback sources are covered by the API surface but not by the differential corpus.
claims.limitation: Stated as a limitation rather than a strength. Both transcript producers drive json_open_buffer, because it is the source that takes a fixed byte array and is therefore reproducible. json_open_stream and json_open_user are implemented, exported, and exercised by tests/original/abi_consumer.c and the upstream suite, but not compared transcript-by-transcript. Extending the harness to the FILE* source is the most valuable next step.

claims.text: On the independent nst/JSONTestSuite conformance corpus, the Zig port and the pinned C original agree on all 318 parsing cases across 5 drive modes, and the original is fully conforming (95/95 must-accept, 188/188 must-reject).
claims.limitation: JSONTestSuite is MIT-licensed and fetched on demand rather than vendored, so this step is skipped when it is absent and `make verify` still succeeds offline; the generated report is committed as evidence. The corpus is used to separate 'the port is wrong' from 'the original is wrong' from 'the standard leaves it open' -- it is not a pass/fail gate on the port. Its i_ cases are implementation-defined and counted as conforming either way.

claims.text: No divergence has ever been observed on any input where the pinned original is well defined: 1,926 fixed-corpus comparisons plus 1,590 JSONTestSuite comparisons plus the published fuzz session, all at zero.
claims.limitation: Scoped to the buffer input source (see C-18) and to the host and CI targets. 'Well defined' is decided mechanically by an ASan+UBSan build of the original, not by judgement (DECISIONS.md D-16).

claims.text: Differential fuzzing found a real defect in this port -- a one-ULP hex-float rounding error in json_get_number -- which is fixed, regression-tested, and documented.
claims.limitation: Found at ~30 million cases in the published session against an earlier build. The minimized 22-byte reproducer is committed as fixture regress-fuzz-hexfloat-stale-buffer and as two tests in tests/port/regressions.zig. Root cause and fix in DECISIONS.md D-18. Reported here because a fuzzer that has never found anything is not evidence that anything was checked.
